    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.Combinatorics.Quiver.TotalPath, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Indexed quiver paths, concatenation, and reversal #

    LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath Q records a path of a quiver together with its source and target. Two such paths can be concatenated when the target of the second is the source of the first. The partial operation LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.mul? records this condition with an Option result, using the later-factor-first order: x.mul? y traces y and then x.

    Concatenation adds path lengths and keeps the source of the factor written second — the one traced first — so it is the trivial path at a vertex exactly when both its factors are. It is associative as a partial operation, and trivial paths are left and right units at the appropriate endpoints. These operations supply the path index and multiplication of the path algebra, independently of any coefficient semiring.

    When the quiver has arrow reversal, indexed paths can also be reversed, exchanging their source and target and reversing the order of partial concatenation. Involutive arrow reversal makes path reversal involutive.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath: the total space Σ a b, Quiver.Path a b of paths.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?: concatenation when the paths meet, and none otherwise.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.reverse: reversal of an indexed path, including its endpoints.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.finite_of_finite_totalPath: a quiver with finitely many indexed paths has finitely many vertices.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.eq_nil_iff: a path is trivial at a vertex exactly when it starts there and has length zero.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_eq_none_iff: concatenation is undefined exactly when the endpoints do not meet.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.length_eq_add_of_mul?_eq_some and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.fst_of_mul?_eq_some: concatenation adds lengths and keeps the source of the factor written second, which is traced first.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.eq_nil_iff_of_mul?_eq_some: a concatenation is the trivial path at a vertex exactly when both its factors are.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_nil_left, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_nil_right, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.mul?_assoc: trivial-path units and associativity.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.map_reverse_mul?: reversal reverses the order of partial concatenation.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.Quiver.TotalPath.mk_cons_eq_mk_cons_iff: a path into a vertex is determined by its last arrow and the path before it.

    References #

    Assem--Simson--Skowroński, Elements of the Representation Theory of Associative Algebras I, Ch. II.
